name.text: 01 Question: Positive vs Negative Apparatus Structure

questiontext.text: <p>What distinguishes a 'positive apparatus' from a 'negative apparatus' in classical textual criticism?</p>

answer.text: <p>A positive apparatus explicitly cites the witnesses that support the lemma as well as the variant readings, whereas a negative apparatus lists only the dissenting witnesses, assuming all others support the lemma.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. A positive apparatus explicitly enumerates witnesses for the lemma, providing total clarity at the expense of typographical space, whereas a negative apparatus only lists variants.</p>

answer.text: <p>A positive apparatus only records pleasant or inspiring passages, whereas a negative apparatus records tragic events.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The terms refer to explicit versus implicit witness citation, not emotional or literary tone.</p>

answer.text: <p>A positive apparatus is used exclusively for printed books, whereas a negative apparatus is used for digital websites.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Both conventions originated in print textual editing and are modeled in digital TEI editions.</p>

answer.text: <p>A positive apparatus requires approval from an ecclesiastical council, whereas a negative apparatus is secular.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The distinction is purely structural and philological.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>In the TEI parallel segmentation method, what is the required structural hierarchy for encoding a textual variant?</p>

answer.text: <p>The <app> element contains a single optional <lem> (lemma) followed by one or more <rdg> (reading) elements.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. In TEI P5, <app> groups the variation point, enclosing <lem> for the preferred reading and <rdg> for each witness variation.</p>

answer.text: <p>The <lem> element encloses several child <app> elements, each containing a <choice>.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <app> is the parent container, not <lem>.</p>

answer.text: <p><rdg> encloses <lem>, which in turn encloses <sourceDesc>.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <sourceDesc> belongs in the teiHeader, and <rdg> cannot enclose <lem>.</p>

answer.text: <p>All variants must be written inside an HTML <footnote> tag without XML elements.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. TEI uses structured semantic tags (<app>, <lem>, <rdg>) rather than presentation footnotes.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>In a TEI critical edition, how should the `@wit` attribute on a `<rdg>` element reference a specific manuscript witness?</p>

answer.text: <p>With a URI hash pointer (e.g. `wit="#ms-A"`) corresponding to an `xml:id="ms-A"` declared on a `<witness>` element in the header's `<listWit>`.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. In TEI, @wit uses IDREF URI syntax (prefixed with `#`) resolving directly to a unique xml:id defined in <listWit>.</p>

answer.text: <p>With a free-text sentence describing the library shelf in plain prose.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Structured attributes require formal ID pointers for automated processing.</p>

answer.text: <p>By writing the full binary file path to the witness on the editor's local Mac hard drive.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Pointers must be portable relative URIs, not machine-specific local paths.</p>

answer.text: <p>By omitting the attribute entirely and letting the web browser guess the manuscript.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Omitting @wit makes the apparatus anonymous and untraceable.</p>

name.text: 04 Question: Three TEI Apparatus Attachment Methods

questiontext.text: <p>Which of the following represents the three recognized TEI methods for linking a critical apparatus to a text?</p>

answer.text: <p>Parallel segmentation, location-referenced method, and double-endpoint attachment.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. TEI P5 Chapter 12 officially defines these three methods for apparatus encoding.</p>

answer.text: <p>Git commit, Git push, and Git pull.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are version control operations, not TEI apparatus encoding methods.</p>

answer.text: <p>Bitmap, vector, and JPEG compression.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are digital image formats.</p>

answer.text: <p>HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are web development technologies.</p>

name.text: 05 Question: Purpose of the TEI Critical Apparatus Toolbox

questiontext.text: <p>What is the primary function of the TEI Critical Apparatus Toolbox developed by Marjorie Burghart?</p>

answer.text: <p>It processes TEI XML files containing critical apparatus markup to visualize witness comparisons, generate apparatus statistics, and check sigla consistency.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. The Toolbox provides specialized online tools to display parallel segmentation, inspect variant distribution, and validate witness lists.</p>

answer.text: <p>It automatically translates ancient Greek poetry into modern Canadian English.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The Toolbox analyzes markup structure and variant distribution, not machine translation.</p>

answer.text: <p>It scans physical manuscripts using a computer webcam.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. It is a web-based analytical tool for processing encoded TEI XML documents.</p>

answer.text: <p>It acts as an antivirus firewall for Moodle servers.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. It is an editorial digital humanities tool, not network security software.</p>

name.text: 06 Question: Transforming CollateX Data into TEI Apparatus

questiontext.text: <p>When transforming a CollateX alignment matrix into a TEI `<app>` entry, how is a cell where a witness lacks text represented?</p>

answer.text: <p>As an empty `<rdg wit="#witX"/>` element or an `<rdg wit="#witX"><gap reason="omitted"/></rdg>` element representing an omission.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. An alignment gap in CollateX indicates that the witness omits the token, encoded in TEI as an empty <rdg> or explicit omission marker.</p>

answer.text: <p>By deleting the witness entirely from the `<teiHeader>`.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Witnesses that omit a phrase remain part of the edition and must be accounted for.</p>

answer.text: <p>By substituting text from an entirely different poem.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Splicing unrelated text violates textual scholarship.</p>

answer.text: <p>By halting the transformation script and throwing a fatal error.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Omissions are standard variant phenomena handled routinely by alignment scripts.</p>

name.text: 07 Question: Complex Variants with Corrections in Witnesses

questiontext.text: <p>How can a TEI apparatus entry represent that a variant reading in Witness B was added by a second scribal hand (`#hand2`) after an earlier reading was erased?</p>

answer.text: <p><rdg wit="#witB"><subst><del>original_text</del><add hand="#hand2">corrected_text</add></subst></rdg></p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. TEI modularity allows primary-source alteration elements (<subst>, <del>, <add>) to be nested directly inside apparatus <rdg> containers.</p>

answer.text: <p><app><error>correction_occurred</error></app></p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <error> is not a valid TEI apparatus element.</p>

answer.text: <p>By writing a footnote in Microsoft Word and pasting a screenshot into the XML file.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. TEI editions use semantic XML markup, not raster screenshot images.</p>

answer.text: <p>By creating two completely separate TEI documents and never linking them.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Apparatus markup explicitly unifies variant readings in a single comparative structure.</p>

name.text: 08 Question: AI Hallucinations in Critical Apparatus Drafting

questiontext.text: <p>When an LLM is asked to draft a TEI critical apparatus from collated tables, what is a frequent hallucination defect?</p>

answer.text: <p>Inventing non-existent manuscript sigla (phantom witnesses) or silently dropping dissenting witnesses from the `<rdg>` list.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Generative models struggle with rigid accounting across tables, often dropping rare witnesses or fabricating plausible-looking sigla not in the source.</p>

answer.text: <p>Formatting the XML using valid hexadecimal color codes.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Color formatting is not a typical apparatus hallucination.</p>

answer.text: <p>Refusing to output anything unless paid in cryptocurrency.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. LLMs do not solicit cryptocurrency in code generation prompts.</p>

answer.text: <p>Encrypting the witness names using RSA-2048 encryption.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Models produce text, not cryptographic ciphertexts, unless explicitly asked.</p>

name.text: 09 Question: Advantages of Digital Parallel Segmentation over Print

questiontext.text: <p>Why is the digital parallel segmentation method considered methodologically superior to traditional printed apparatus footnotes?</p>

answer.text: <p>It embeds variants directly at their exact point of occurrence in the text hierarchy, eliminating ambiguous footnote reference numbers and arbitrary print space constraints.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Parallel segmentation keeps the text and variants tightly coupled in machine-actionable XML, enabling dynamic multi-view rendering without print space compromises.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because digital editions are completely free of all copyright restrictions worldwide.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital editions are subject to licensing and copyright laws like any scholarly publication.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because digital files can never be deleted from a computer once written.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital files require active preservation and backups.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because printed books are no longer permitted in university libraries.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Print books remain vital scholarly resources.</p>

name.text: 10 Question: Quality Assurance Checklist for Apparatus XML

questiontext.text: <p>Before finalizing a digital critical apparatus for publication, what verification step is essential?</p>

answer.text: <p>Validating the XML against the TEI schema and verifying that 100% of the `@wit` pointers resolve to declared witnesses in `<listWit>`.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Schema validation guarantees syntactic well-formedness, while pointer integrity auditing ensures no dangling or invalid witness references exist.</p>

answer.text: <p>Confirming that every manuscript in the world agrees with the editor's personal interpretation.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Witnesses naturally disagree; the goal is accurate documentation, not forced unanimity.</p>

answer.text: <p>Deleting the `<teiHeader>` to reduce file download size for mobile users.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The teiHeader contains vital metadata and witness declarations that cannot be removed.</p>

answer.text: <p>Replacing all polytonic Greek characters with Latin transliterations.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scholarly digital editions preserve authentic original scripts using Unicode.</p>
